parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The module is the infrastructure/adapter layer and does one job: provide concrete adapters for the application and domain ports, then wire them up.
- in-memory-repositories.ts implements the domain repository interfaces (UserRepository, ProjectRepository, TaskRepository).
- system-adapters.ts implements the application ports (IdGenerator, Clock).
- http-app.ts is the inbound HTTP adapter. It talks only to AppServices (UserService, ProjectService, TaskService).
- server.ts is the composition root that wires all of them together.

The module uses its abstractions consistently:
- http-app.ts calls the services rather than the repositories.
- Task-status validation calls the domain's isTaskStatus and TASK_STATUSES instead of keeping its own list of statuses.
- server.ts injects the adapters through constructors.

No rule is duplicated in a way the source shows. The task filter logic appears only once, in InMemoryTaskRepository.findByProject, and the mapping from errors to HTTP status codes appears only once, in createApp's error middleware. http-app.ts does check request shape (requiredString/optionalString), but that is parsing at the HTTP boundary, not copied domain rules. The service code isn't included, so I can't confirm the services don't repeat these checks.
